 Arsenal vs Everton LIVE: Premier League latest score, match stream, goal updates and fan reaction
 Gunners go in search of third straight Premier League win 
 LIVE: Arsenal vs Everton Getty Tashan Deniran-Alleyne | Matt Verri , Football Reporter at Emirates Stadium 1 minute ago Arsenal vs Everton LIVE
 Premier League football is back in N5 this afternoon as Arsenal host Everton. It is a third game in six days for the Gunners and confidence in the squad should be high having responded to defeat at Brighton before the international break by putting together a four-game unbeaten run, including a 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League last time out.
 Mikel Arteta, though, has been dealt a major blow after Bukayo Saka sustained a quad injury inside 10 minutes at the Allianz Arena and will be sidelined indefinitely. The winger joins Christos Tzolis and William Saliba on the sidelines, but Piero Hincapie has made a swift recovery from an ankle issue and returns to the Arsenal matchday squad.

Follow the game LIVE below with Standard Sport's dedicated match blog, featuring expert insight and analysis from Matt Verri at the Emirates Stadium.

 Live updates
 Arsenal 2-0 Everton
 71 min: There was VAR check before Gabriel’s goal was given. White clearly onside. Everton make a change as Dibling replaces Johnson.
 Matt Verri at Emirates Stadium
 Not a set-piece but it is another centre-back goal for Arsenal. Perfect cross from White and Gabriel, who we can safely say has recovered from that earlier issue, is not missing from there. 
 GOAL! Arsenal 2-0 Everton | Gabriel ‘68
 68 min: ARSENAL MAKE IT TWO
 Gabriel and Havertz queuing up at the back post to meet White’s cross, the Brazilian makes contact and beats Pickford.
 Arsenal 1-0 Everton
 67 min: Arsenal make a triple change before the corner.
 Gyokeres, Lewis-Skelly and Merino make way for Havertz, Guimaraes and Calafiori.
 Arsenal 1-0 Everton
 66 min: Really good play from Gyokeres as he holds off Armstrong and gets Arsenal going, Madueke finds Merino in space but the midfielder is closed down by Tarkowski.
 Arsenal 1-0 Everton
 65 min: Another yellow card, this time for Garner after the Everton midfielder caught Merino late.
 Matt Verri at Emirates Stadium
 Arteta walked back to his seat when he saw the referee coming, made himself look busy, turned away... those efforts are not enough for him to avoid being shown a yellow card. 
 Arsenal 1-0 Everton
 63 min: Mikel Arteta booked.
 Arsenal 1-0 Everton
 61 min: Eze takes on Rohl on the outside and flashes in a cross looking for Gyokeres in the middle, but Pickford is quick off his line to smother the ball.
 Arsenal 1-0 Everton
 59 min: Lewis-Skelly has his name taken for pulling back Johnson.
 Everton free-kick is deep but White makes first contact and Arsenal are able to push up.
